 Lakers expect to have to manage Adou Thiero’s minutes all season
 The second-year forward has dealt with knee injuries for a few seasons now
 by Jackson Frank Nov 17, 2026, 6:23 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Much like his rookie year, Adou Thiero has been in and out of the lineup to begin 2026-27 as he navigates knee issues. After playing 25 games last season — a mix of injuries and being buried in the rotation — he’s appeared in four games this year. When he has played, his athleticism, off-ball instincts and offensive rebounding have all popped.
 But Thiero’s knee problems span back to college and have persisted through one-plus years in the NBA, so Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick understands the organization must be careful in how it handles his playing time.
 “We’re going to have to just naturally manage his minutes all season. We’ll just have to,” Redick told reporters pre-game on Sunday. “And so we’ve tried to play, at times, an 11-man rotation and sometimes that means maybe a four- or five-minute run in the first half and that’s it for him. ... In his minutes, I think he’s been really good. We want him crashing. We want him putting pressure on the rim as a roller and a cutter. We want him out in transition.”
 Thiero injects the Lakers with welcomed athletic juice, strength and speed in their forward rotation, though his scoring, shooting and health worries do mean they must be precise in how they deploy his skill-set. It’s evident how he can help, however, largely behind the strain he puts on defenses with paint touches:
 Thiero was available for Sunday’s win over the Phoenix Suns but did not play (he logged minutes in the prior four games, though). He is not listed on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Charlotte Hornets either. With Austin Reaves still out because of a bruised heel and Walker Kessler now also sidelined because of right lower leg soreness, it seems plausible Thiero rejoins the rotation to soak up some front-court minutes, where Los Angeles will need reinforcements.
 The Lakers will aim to extend their winning streak to nine games when they take on the Hornets at 8 p.m. Thiero, meanwhile, will hope he gets a chance to show what he brings to the table for this team.
